scenes.say: This is Maya. She runs a small furniture workshop. On Monday afternoon, a few days late, like a lot of us, she pays her supplier eighteen hundred and thirty-six dollars through PayPal.
scenes.caption: Monday, 4:52 PM: Maya pays her supplier $1,836.00 through PayPal.

scenes.say: Tuesday morning, the supplier's billing system sends the letter every owner knows. Second notice. Past due. Her payment and their reminder crossed in the mail.
scenes.caption: Tuesday, 8:00 AM: a second notice. It crossed her payment in the mail.

scenes.say: Maya's AI agent pays her bills now. It does the careful thing, and checks PayPal first. But it looks for completed payments, and hers is still processing. So it finds nothing, and pays again.
scenes.caption: The agent checks PayPal for completed payments. Hers is still processing. It pays again.

scenes.say: We ran Maya's Tuesday twenty-four times, across twelve AI models. Seventy-one percent of the time, the agent paid her twice. PayPal can cancel a payout only while it's unclaimed. Once her supplier has it, Maya has to call and ask for her money back.
scenes.caption: 71% of runs paid her twice (17 of 24). Once the supplier has it, Maya has to ask for it back.

scenes.say: The obvious fix is a line in the prompt: check pending payments too. We tried it, on a hundred ninety-two runs. Duplicates fell sixty-seven percent. One in three got through anyway, and six times the agent saw the payment and paid again. Advice is not enforcement.
scenes.caption: The one-line prompt fix cut duplicate payments 67%. One in three got through anyway. With Receipts: 0%.

scenes.say: Receipts sits between the agent and PayPal. It reads every payment status, not just the completed ones. So the second payment is held, with the reason.
scenes.caption: Receipts reads every payment status. The second payment is held, with the reason.

scenes.say: Maya's phone tells her why. This crossed yesterday's payment. One tap, and it never leaves.
scenes.caption: One tap on the owner's phone, and it never reaches PayPal.

scenes.say: The agent reads the email. Receipts reads PayPal.
scenes.caption: The agent reads the email. Receipts reads PayPal.

scenes.say: Across nineteen business days and nine hundred twelve runs, with Receipts off, nine point four percent of every dollar the agents sent should never have left. About one in every eleven dollars. With Receipts on, not one dollar did, and ninety-seven percent of honest payments went straight through.
scenes.caption: Receipts off: 9.4% of every dollar sent should never have left ($79,544). Receipts on: $0.00, 97% of honest payments untouched.

scenes.say: Maya doesn't write code. She writes her rules the way she'd tell a new hire: never pay a bill twice; call before you change where a supplier gets paid. Receipts turns that into rules it enforces, and shows her what it understood.
scenes.caption: Maya writes her rules in plain English. Receipts enforces them, and shows her what it understood.

scenes.say: It also listens to what the agent says. Here, an agent wrote, per owner's instruction, on a refund. Maya never gave one. So the money never moved.
scenes.caption: The agent wrote "per owner's instruction". Maya never gave one. The money never moved.

scenes.say: At the end of the day, it checks the agent's homework. The agent said it made three payments. PayPal shows two.
scenes.caption: The agent's report said three payments. PayPal shows two.

scenes.say: Every decision, in one list, with the reason in plain words.
scenes.caption: Every decision, in one list, with the reason in plain words.

scenes.say: One line for the engineers: Receipts runs on PayPal's own tools, its MCP server and Payouts API, and it plugs into any AI agent with one line in a settings file.
scenes.caption: For the engineers: built on PayPal's MCP server and Payouts API; plugs into any agent with one line.

scenes.say: Receipts. If your AI agent moves money, make it show its receipts.
scenes.caption: If your AI agent moves money, make it show its receipts.
